corrections.governor: Nicolas Gutierrez granted El Molino (1836); Figueroa granted only the exchanged-away Ojotska tract (Dec 1833). Per petition transcript p4 and Vallejo deposition transcript p7; Hoffman corroborates 'Feb. 24th 1836, by Nicolas Gutierrez'.

notes: El Molino / Rio Ojotska (Cooper), a two-grant exchange. (1) Rio Ojotska (aka Rio del Sacramento) granted by Figueroa, decreed Dec 23 1833 / título Dec 31 1833, Deputation-approved May 17 1834 (expediente 'A'/'B', transcript p16-29). Cooper found it inconvenient and EXCHANGED it with the government for (2) El Molino (Levanta hyeme) in Sonoma Co., granted by Nicolas Gutierrez in 1836. The register's rancho 'Molinos' + year 1836 track the El Molino grant, but its governor 'Jose Figueroa' belongs to the surrendered Ojotska tract, hence governor ERR = Gutierrez. Hoffman lists both ('1833 by Figueroa, and Feb 24 1836 by Nicolas Gutierrez'). The El Molino título itself ('C'/'D', Gutierrez) sits later in the transcript than the ~35 pages read but is verbatim recited in the petition (p4) and by Vallejo (p7). Claim confirmed by the Board Nov 14 1854.

notes: Monte del Diablo (Salvio Pacheco). The expediente 'B' carries a long 1828 back-history: Pacheco first petitioned (San Diego, Oct 31 1828, under Echeandía) and feuded with an Englishman Guillermo/Julian Willis over the site (Laguna de los Bolbones). The operative confirmed GRANT, however, is the Figueroa título dated July 26, 1834. Both the register (1836) and Hoffman (1844) misstate the year; the case file is unambiguously 1834. Governor (Figueroa) and grantee (Salvio Pacheco) correct. Board confirmed 4 sq leagues Jan 5 1853; US appealed Aug 1854; later patented (Phase C).

year.evidence: The definitive confirmed grants are dated April 27, 1842, not 1837. Both títulos ('B', annexed to Hartnell depo): Olivera título 'Dado en Monterey á veinte y siete de Abril de mil ochocientos cuarenta y dos. Juan B. Alvarado. Manuel Jimeno Srio' (transcript p17); Feliz título identical date 'veinte y siete de Abril de mil ochocientos cuarenta y dos' (transcript p20); petition (transcript p4) 'both bearing date the twenty seventh of April A.D. 1842.' The '1837' matches only the earlier PROVISIONAL concession by Alvarado (Dec 28, 1837; expediente 'E' header '1837', transcript p8/p13/p15), which is interim and not the grant McKinley claims/was patented under.

governor.evidence: Both definitive títulos signed 'Juan B. Alvarado Gobernador Constitucional del Departamento de las Californias' (transcript p17, p20); the 1837 provisional concession also 'Alvarado' (transcript p11/p14). James (Santiago) McKinley is the PURCHASER/claimant, not the grantee: petition (transcript p4) 'both of said grantees (Martin Olveria and Vicente Feliz) did transfer unto your Petitioner...'; deed 'C' (transcript p22, San Luis Obispo Nov 20 1845) conveys from Vicente Feliz to 'Dn Santiago McKinley'; Olivera's deed dated Oct 27 1846. Hoffman also gives grantee 'Martin Olivera.'

corrections.grantee: Original grantees Martín Olivera (El Morro) and Vicente Feliz (Los Cayucos), per Alvarado April 27 1842; James/Santiago McKinley bought both parcels (Feliz deed Nov 20 1845, transcript p22; Olivera deed Oct 27 1846).

notes: Morro y Cayucos (Case 155 SD, Comm. No. 529). Rancho = two adjacent one-league tracts: El Morro (to Martín Olivera) and Los Cayucos (to Vicente Feliz), BOTH definitively granted by Gov. Juan B. Alvarado on April 27, 1842 (títulos 'B'). Grantees first got a PROVISIONAL/interim concession from Alvarado in 1837 (expediente 'E', which is headed '1837') — the register's '1837'. James (Santiago) McKinley is the claimant who purchased both parcels (1845/1846) and prosecuted the claim. So year ERR (1842 is the confirmed grant) and grantee ERR (Olivera + Feliz, not McKinley); governor Alvarado and rancho name are correct. Hoffman agrees on 1842 and lists grantee Martin Olivera. Board confirmed Apr 4 1854; US appealed Aug 1854; patented later (Phase C).

name.evidence: This grant genuinely has NO rancho name. p1 red cover label 'CASE NO. 143 NORTHERN DISTRICT / A TRACT OF LAND NEAR SANTA CLARA GRANT / JAMES ENRIGHT CLAIMANT'; transcript title p1 'for the place named A tract of land near Santa Clara'; petition (transcript p6) 'a tract of land 2000 varas square near to the Mission of Santa Clara.' Register's placeholder 'Unnamed grant (ND 143)' correctly reflects an unnamed tract; Hoffman's 'name' field is a garbled '2' (i.e. the 2000-vara dimension).

year.evidence: Grant made in 1845. Petition (transcript p6): Garcia petitioned Micheltorena Dec 26 1844; 'on the same day to wit the 6th day of January 1845, said Governor granted the same to the said Garcia'; Salvio Pacheco depo (transcript p8): 'a Petition of Francisco Garcia for land with a decree of Governor Micheltorena on it dated January 16th 1845'; Forbes depo (transcript p10) 'heard in 1845 of the existence of the grant.' Register 1845 correct (Hoffman also 1845). Minor day discrepancy 6th vs 16th Jan; grant document Exhibit A/B sits further in the 300-pp file.

governor.evidence: Grant by 'Don Manuel Micheltorena the Governor and Superior Political Chief of the Department of California' (petition transcript p6); Pacheco depo (transcript p8) 'a decree of Governor Micheltorena.' Register 'Micheltorena' correct.

grantee.evidence: The grantee was FRANCISCO GARCIA, not James Enright. Petition (transcript p6): 'said Governor granted the same to the said Garcia as asked for'; (transcript p7) 'some time in the year 1847 the said Garcia sold and conveyed said land to your Petitioner [Enright]... another conveyance... executed... by said Garcia on the 16th day of November 1848.' Enright is the purchaser/claimant. Hoffman lists grantee 'Francisco Garcia.' Forbes depo (transcript p10): 'the purchase of the land by him [Enright] from Francisco Garcia.'
